## Incident Report — NetSupport RAT Infection (2024-11-26 capture)

### Victim host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.11.26.183** | Consistent source IP across all suspicious flows |
| MAC | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | Ethernet source address on frames from 10.11.26.183 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (workgroup/domain view: NEMOTODES) | NBNS Name Query/Registration for 10.11.26.183 (`<00>` Workstation, `<20>` Server service) |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic from 10.11.26.183 to DC 10.11.26.3 |
| AD domain | nemotodes.health, DC = NEMOTODE-DC (10.11.26.3) | NBNS `NEMOTODE-DC<20>`, SMB2/DCERPC paths referencing `nemotodes.health\Policies\...` |

### Malware family
**NetSupport RAT (malicious use of the NetSupport Manager remote-access client)**
**Attribution: signature-confirmed.**
- Suricata alerts fire directly on the family: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin/Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
- Independently confirmed in the raw capture: every C2 POST carries `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, and the beacon bodies use the literal NetSupport client-server protocol tokens `CMD=POLL / INFO=1 / ACK=1` and `CMD=ENCD / ES=1 / DATA=<hex>`.

### Delivery chain (observed, timestamps UTC)
1. 04:50:11 — DNS + TLS session to **classicgrand.com** (213.246.109.5) — redirector/landing hop.
2. 04:50:14 — DNS + TLS session to **modandcrackedapk.com** (193.42.38.139) — fake "cracked APK/software" lure page (flagged by Suricata as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup / TLS SNI`).
3. 04:50:14 — DNS to **confirmsubscription.com** (13.56.30.207, 52.8.34.0) — ad/redirect infrastructure tied to the same lure chain.
4. 04:50:45 — victim queries **geo.netsupportsoftware.com** (104.26.1.231) and receives a geolocation (`GET /location/loca.asp` → `33.7488,-84.3877`) — the NetSupport client's own first-run geolocation check, confirming client-side execution around this time.
5. 04:50:45 onward — C2 beaconing begins to **194.180.191.64:443** via plaintext HTTP `POST /fakeurl.htm` (labeled port 443 but not TLS — flagged by Suricata as `ET POLICY HTTP traffic on port 443 (POST)` / `HTTP POST on unusual Port Possibly Hostile`), repeating roughly every 60 seconds through at least 05:43:29 UTC, the end of the observed activity window.

The delivery sessions to classicgrand.com and modandcrackedapk.com are TLS-encrypted, so the exact download URL, dropped file name, and file hash of the NetSupport client installer could not be recovered from this capture — no decryption keys were available and no plaintext file transfer was observed. This is stated honestly rather than guessed.

### Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| c2_endpoint | **194.180.191.64:443** | Repeated `POST /fakeurl.htm`, `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, `CMD=POLL/ENCD` bodies; matches ETPRO NetSupport RAT CnC alerts |
| url | `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` | Same as above, ~60s beacon interval |
| domain | **modandcrackedapk.com** → 193.42.38.139 | DNS query + TLS SNI at 04:50:14, flagged `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain` (fake cracked-software lure) |
| domain | **classicgrand.com** → 213.246.109.5 | DNS query + TLS SNI at 04:50:11, first hop of the redirect chain preceding the lure site |
| domain | **confirmsubscription.com** → 13.56.30.207, 52.8.34.0 | DNS query at 04:50:14, same redirect/lure timeframe |
| domain (abused legitimate infra) | geo.netsupportsoftware.com → 104.26.1.231 | `GET /location/loca.asp`, NetSupport client's built-in geolocation check, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request` |

No file name or SHA256 could be grounded in the capture — the delivery payload transfer occurred entirely inside TLS sessions.

### Benign context (not IOCs)
- Standard Windows/Office telemetry and update traffic: `windowsupdate.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `officeapps.live.com`, `resources.office.net`, `smartscreen.microsoft.com`, `msn.com`, `bing.com`, `wns.windows.com`, MSN/Bing/Office CDN hosts.
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` / `armmf.adobe.com` GET `ProcessMAU.txt` — Adobe update-manager check-in, unrelated to the infection.
- Internal AD/domain traffic: Kerberos, LDAP/CLDAP, SMB2/DCERPC/SAMR to DC 10.11.26.3 (NEMOTODE-DC), group-policy file pulls (`GptTmpl.inf`, `Registry.pol`, `gpt.ini`) — normal domain-joined workstation behavior, though the earlier SMBv1/NTLMSSP alerts on this same session are worth a separate hygiene note (legacy SMBv1 in use) even though they are not part of this malware chain.
- ARP/NBNS/SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR broadcast noise typical of a Windows LAN.

### Incident summary
The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user **oboomwald** on the **nemotodes.health** AD domain, was infected with the **NetSupport RAT** after browsing through a redirect chain (classicgrand.com → modandcrackedapk.com, a fake cracked-software/APK site → confirmsubscription.com) starting at 04:50 UTC on 2024-11-26. Shortly after, the NetSupport client performed its self-geolocation lookup and began persistent HTTP C2 beaconing to **194.180.191.64:443** (`POST /fakeurl.htm`, User-Agent `NetSupport Manager/1.3`) roughly every 60 seconds for over 50 minutes, giving the attacker an active remote-access channel into the host.
